report: A 2-year-old boy with a femoral diaphyseal fracture shows a diffuse sclerosing survey: cranial/facial hyperostosis, rib/clavicle sclerosis, femoral hyperostosis with stress fractures, hand/foot dysplasia, and bilateral optic canal narrowing. Independent radiologic and laboratory experts refute non-accidental trauma, metabolic bone disease, pathological fracture, and classic osteogenesis imperfecta. This indicates genetic bone fragility, best fitting sclerosing skeletal dysplasia, pending genetic confirmation.
